import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Eighth root of the generating function of an Apéry-like sequence

The auxiliary sequence used for the Hankel matrix, defined as
$$\sum_{k=0}^n \binom{n}{k}^2 \binom{n+k}{k}^2$$

Determinant of the $(n+1) \times (n+1)$ Hankel-type matrix with
$(i,j)$-entry equal to A005259$(i+j)$ for all $i,j = 0,\dots,n$.
The entry function A005259 is taken to be $\sum_{k=0}^n \binom{n}{k}^2 \binom{n+k}{k}^2$.

*References:*
- [A228143](https://oeis.org/A228143)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
- [A005259](https://oeis.org/A005259)
-/

namespace OeisA228143


open Polynomial

open BigOperators Matrix Nat

/--
The auxiliary sequence used for the Hankel matrix, defined as
$$\sum_{k=0}^n \binom{n}{k}^2 \binom{n+k}{k}^2$$
-/
def aperyLike (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Finset.sum (Finset.range (n + 1)) fun k =>
    (n.choose k)^2 * ((Nat.choose (n + k) k))^2

/--
Determinant of the $(n+1) \times (n+1)$ Hankel-type matrix with
$(i,j)$-entry equal to A005259$(i+j)$ for all $i,j = 0,\dots,n$.
The entry function A005259 is taken to be $\sum_{k=0}^n \binom{n}{k}^2 \binom{n+k}{k}^2$.
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  let dim : Type := Fin (n + 1)
  -- Matrix entries are lifted to ℤ for determinant calculation
  let M : Matrix dim dim ℤ :=
    Matrix.of fun i j => (aperyLike (i.val + j.val) : ℤ)
  -- The sequence is known to be non-negative integers (nonn).
  M.det.natAbs

open PowerSeries

/-- The power series $A(x/3) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{a(n)}{3^n} x^n$ over ℚ. -/
def ogfAScaled : PowerSeries ℚ :=
  PowerSeries.mk fun n => (a n : ℚ) / (3 ^ n : ℚ)


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by native_decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_1 : a 1 = 48 := by native_decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_2 : a 2 = 161856 := by native_decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_3 : a 3 = 39002646528 := by native_decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 674708032182398976 := by native_decide


/--
Conjecture: if $A(x) = 1 + 48x + 161856 x^2 + \cdots$ denotes the o.g.f. then $A(x/3)^{1/8}$ has integer coefficients. - _Peter Bala_, Apr 22 2018

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/228143.wip.lean#L698"]
theorem exists_power_series_eighth_pow_eq : ∃ C : PowerSeries ℤ,
    (PowerSeries.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)) (C ^ 8) = ogfAScaled := by
    sorry

end OeisA228143

reformulations.difference: The source defines an integer Hankel determinant, whereas Lean returns its natural absolute value, M.det.natAbs.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Edgar's Theorem 1 gives the exact Apéry sequence used here as s_m = ∫₀ᶜ x^m φ(x) dx, with c > 0 and a positive integrable density. Consequently the Hankel matrix (s_{i+j}) is the Gram matrix of 1,x,…,x^n for this measure. A nonzero polynomial has positive squared integral, so this matrix is positive definite and its determinant is positive. Thus taking natAbs preserves every determinant; after the canonical integer cast, Lean's sequence equals the source's sequence.

reformulations.difference: Instead of stating that the normalized series A(x/3)^(1/8) has integer coefficients, Lean asserts the existence of an integral series C whose eighth power maps to ogfAScaled, without explicitly requiring C's constant coefficient to be 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The scaled series has constant coefficient a(0)=1. Any integral witness therefore has constant coefficient c with c^8=1, hence c=±1. Negating a witness with c=-1 preserves its eighth power and makes its constant coefficient 1. The coefficient map preserves powers. Over ℚ[[X]], an eighth root with constant coefficient 1 is unique, so this normalized witness is precisely the root in the source. Conversely, integer coefficients of that root lift coefficientwise to a witness in ℤ[[X]]. The equivalence with existence of a normalized rational root having integer coefficients, together with normalized-root uniqueness, was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without sorry or reliance on the conjecture theorem.

review.notes: Checked all nine declarations. Lean computations reproduce Apéry terms through n=8, signed and absolute Hankel determinants through n=5, and the displayed eighth-root coefficients through degree 5. The n=0 case, inclusive summation bounds, matrix dimension, rational scaling and coefficient maps agree with the source. OEIS and the cited paper corroborate the research-solved tag for Bala's conjecture. The historical proof has the matching statement and no explicit sorry/custom axioms; replay against the supplied newer Mathlib encounters API-compatibility errors, so I do not claim a fresh verification of that historical proof artifact. OEIS pages were Cloudflare-blocked, so their official data mirror was used.
